derived_from.why_derived: Independent review I6 (M1, M2) showed the checker the owner ordered did not enforce what the records claim: rows could cite non-reusable records for any commit, a PR could authorize itself, edit a record, pick its own baseline and config, and run its own checker. Closing those gaps is a necessary consequence of 'enforce van's ledger'. The design (commit scopes, scope bindings, intake commits, base-ref trust, CODEOWNERS) is the integrator's (unit G9a), not separately approved by the owner.

signature_note: The owner answered in a Claude Code session. No device, biometric or cryptographic signature is claimed. This record is not signed-ingress evidence. The owner did not approve each commit or each file.
limits: No signature of any kind is claimed.
The authority is derived: it covers only the listed files in the commits listed in commit_scope (unit G9a on both programme branches), and no other commit.
It does not authorize any product, browser, trading, Jev, Android, Hermes, deploy or storage change, and it does not open any production activation gate.
It may not redefine security, owner-control or money/custody intent. CODEOWNERS names the repository owner for governance paths; it grants no one else anything.
Branch protection (required check, code-owner review) is a GitHub setting outside the repository; this record does not claim it is enabled.
Not reusable: exact paths, exact commits.
